sentences.text: JUDGMENT 1.

The present claim petition under Section 166 of the 'Motor Vehicle Act, 1988' was filed by the claimants/ legal representatives of Sandeep Kumar (hereinafter, 'the deceased') seeking compensation from the respondents on account of fatal injuries received by the deceased in a motor vehicular accident.

2. Important facts of the case as per claim petition are that on 16.11.2019 at about 08:45 a.m., while the deceased Sandeep Kumar along with his friend Happy Sharma was going for his office work from Dadri by motorcycle at a normal speed and on correct side of the road and when the motorcycle reached 300 meters before village Gulistanpur, within the jurisdiction of PS Surajpur,
Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P., all of a sudden, a truck bearing registration number HR74-8715, being driven by respondent no.1 at a high speed, rashly and negligently, without blowing horn, came from back side and hit the motorcycle with a great force.

As a result, both the motorcycle rider fell down a l o n g w i t h m o t o r c y c l e a n d S a n d e e p K u m a r s u s t a i n e d ______________________________________________________________________ grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Sharda Hospital, Gautam Budh Nagar, where he was declared brought dead and his postmortem was conducted vide postmortem report no.1306/2019,
dated 16.11.2019.
3.

In connection with the accident, the FIR no.1708/2019, under sections 279/304-A/338/427 IPC was registered at PS Surajpur, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. on the same day of accident on the statement of Manoj Kumar, brother of the deceased.
During investigation, it was found out that at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3.

After completion of the investigation,
charge-sheet was filed against the respondent no.1 before the concerned court.

With the above facts,
the claimants by filing the present claim petition prayed for compensation of Rs.50 lakh along with interest @ 12% per annum.

4. All the respondents were served with the notice of claim petition, however, however, written statement was filed only on behalf of respondent no.3/ insurance company taking general defences with the contention that the their liability is subject to compliance of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is stated that number of the vehicle was not mentioned in the FIR as per the copy of FIR.
5.

It is the settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &

After going through the record of the case and hearing part final arguments as recorded in order dated 15.01.2025, the Tribunal was of the opinion that to ascertain as to how the truck bearing registration no. HR74-8715 was pinned down as the vehicle with which the accident was caused,
examination of the Investigating Officer and the driver respondent no.1 Rajkumar as well as re-examination of PW2 Happy Sharma was required.
PW2 Happy Sharma was re- examined by this Tribunal as CW1 (Court Witness).

PW2/CW1 was directed vide order dated 25.02.2025 to transmit/
produce whatever treatment documents the witness had regarding his treatment on the date of accident from Sharda Hospital, Greater Noida.
PW2/CW1 did not transmit any document.
The Investigating Officer was examined by this Tribunal inadvertently as CW1.

Despite multiple efforts,
the respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle could not be served with the summons,
therefore, the owner of the offending vehicle/ respondent no.2 Parmit Mehra was examined under section 168 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam and vide order dated 09.03.2026, notice was issued to the Medical Superintendent of Sharda Hospital, Greater Noida, U.P. to transmit the medical record of Mr. Happy Sharma as well as that of the deceased.

On behalf of Sharda Hospital, Shri Parvin was examined as CW2 who proved the MLC no. 8569 dated 06.11.2019, Admission Form, Death Summary, Medical Certificate of cause of death/ Physicians Progress Notes, OPD Prescription Sheet with respect to patient Sundeep i.e., the deceased, who as per the Sharda Hospital was admitted there on 06.11.2019 as a case of RTA and expired during the treatment on the same day.
The said d o c u m e n t s w e r e e x h i b i t e d a s E x . C W 2 / 2 ( c o l l y ) .

The attested copy of MLC, OPD Prescription Sheet and two cash bills of Mr. Sagar Sharma were exhibited as Ex.CW2/4 (colly).
15. Ex.CW2/4 dispel all doubt which were raised because of the cross- examination as done by the Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3/ insurance company of PW2 Happy Sharma on 30.07.2024.

On the basis of Ex.CW2/4 (colly), it is ascertained and proved that on the date of accident i.e., 06.11.2019, Happy Sharma had also received injuries in road traffic accident and on the date of the accident, Happy Sharma was present in Sharda Hospital and therefore, these facts corroborates the version as given by Happy Sharma as PW2 in his examination-in-chief.

Therefore, it is proved that on 06.11.2019 at about 08:30 A.M., the deceased died because of road accident caused by the offending vehicle by hitting the motorcycle which the deceased was riding on which happy Sharma was pillion rider from behind.

sentences.text: The vehicle which is behind any vehicle has to maintain a reasonable distance from the vehicle ahead of it so that even if any emergency brake is applied by the vehicle in front, the driver of the vehicle which is behind could stop the vehicle without hitting the vehicle in front.

As it is not the case of any of the respondents that the deceased suddenly applied brakes because of which the o f f e n d i n g v e h i c l e r a m m e d i n t o t h e m o t o r c y c l e o f t h e ______________________________________________________________________ deceased causing the accident leading to the death of the deceased.

Even if the deceased would have applied sudden breaks and if the offending vehicle hit the motorcycle from behind, the rashness and negligence would be that of the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no.1.
16.

The postmortem report of the deceased, certified copy of which has been placed on record reveals that the deceased was observed to have sustained multiple antemortem injuries and cause of his death has been opined as hemorrhage and shock and respiratory failure due to injuries to lungs and brain and all injuries were opined to be antemortem in nature.

17. Thus, in the light of the above discussion and the evidence brought on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of the preponderance of probabilities that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into fatal injuries to deceased Sandeep Kumar.
Issue no.1 is, accordingly, decided in favour of petitioners.

18. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners herein are held entitled to get compensation,
however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.

As per settled l a w ,
______________________________________________________________________ compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittances.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) AC 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 19. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.

20. In Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
(2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, the relevant guidelines for compensation were laid down in death cases, which have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

In view of the aforesaid judgments, the compensation in the present case has to be ascertained as under:
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased & Application of Multiplier 21.

As per Aadhaar Card of the deceased, a copy of which has been proved on record as Ex.PW1/1, he was born on 18.12.1991, which would mean that on the date of accident on 16.11.2019, the deceased _________________________________________________________
_____________ was 27 years of age.

Accordingly, the multiplier of 17 belonging to the age group 26-30 years shall be applicable (refer: Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Assessment of Income of deceased 22.

In her examination-in-chief which is by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A, PW1 Smt. Shikha, wife of the deceased states that her deceased husband was working as a Sales Executive with Riyansh Section,
X-3/B1, Gali no.2, Brahmpuri, Delhi and was getting Rs.20,000/- per month.

On the contrary, CW1 Happy Sharma, who stated himself to be co-worker of the deceased, deposed that at the time of accident, he was accompanying the deceased as pillion rider on the motorcycle which the deceased was driving.
CW2 stated that on the date of accident, he along with Sandeep (deceased) was going to the office at Surajpur, Noida as they were working together at Denso Company.
CW2 stated that he and deceased used to get salary of Rs.15,000- 16,000/- per month.
CW2 made it clear that he and Sandeep were working in Denso Company for about 6-7 months before the accident.
Further, in her cross-examination, PW1 (wife of the deceased) has fairly admitted that she does not have any document regarding employment and income of her deceased husband.
The Aadhaar Card of the deceased and that of the petitioners show their residential address of Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P.
No document regarding education of the deceased has been placed on record.

In the absence of any documentary evidence regarding vocation, income and education of the deceased, his income has to b e a s s e s s e d a s p e r m i n i m u m w a g e s a p p l i c a b l e t o t h e c a t e g o r y o f u n s k i l l e d ______________________________________________________________________ workers of U.P. on the date of accident (16.11.2019), which were Rs.8,279/- per month.

Hence,
income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.8,279/- per month.

23.

In the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

The accident of the deceased in this case occurred on 16.11.2019, therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further,
in view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co.
Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, claimants are required to be granted spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

opennyai_summary.facts: The present claim petition under Section 166 of the 'Motor Vehicle Act, 1988' was filed by the claimants/ legal representatives of Sandeep Kumar (hereinafter, 'the deceased') seeking compensation from the respondents on account of fatal injuries received by the deceased in a motor vehicular accident.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
12.
Therefore, it is proved that on 06.11.2019 at about 08:30 A.M., the deceased died because of road accident caused by the offending vehicle by hitting the motorcycle which the deceased was riding on which happy Sharma was pillion rider from behind.
The rashness and negligence is writ large in the Shikkha Devi vs Raj Kumar Yadav And Ors on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159321118/
6 manner of the accident i.e., hitting of the motor-cycle of the deceased from behind by the offending vehicle.
The vehicle which is behind any vehicle has to maintain a reasonable distance from the vehicle ahead of it so that even if any emergency brake is applied by the vehicle in front, the driver of the vehicle which is behind could stop the vehicle without hitting the vehicle in front.
Even if the deceased would have applied sudden breaks and if the offending vehicle hit the motorcycle from behind, the rashness and negligence would be that of the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no.1.
16.
The postmortem report of the deceased, certified copy of which has been placed on record reveals that the deceased was observed to have sustained multiple antemortem injuries and cause of his death has been opined as hemorrhage and shock and respiratory failure due to injuries to lungs and brain and all injuries were opined to be antemortem in nature.
17. Thus, in the light of the above discussion and the evidence brought on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of the preponderance of probabilities that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into fatal injuries to deceased Sandeep Kumar.
18. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners herein are held entitled to get compensation,
however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) AC 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 19. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
20. In Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
(2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, the relevant guidelines for compensation were laid down in death cases, which have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
The deceased was 27 years of age.
In this case, the deceased left behind his wife, three minor children, mother and one unmarried sister, who are the petitioners herein.
Father of the deceased is stated to be predeceased.

rpc_texts: Issue no.1 is, accordingly, decided in favour of petitioners.

The accident of the deceased in this case occurred on 16.11.2019, therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Accordingly, petitioner no.1 being wife of the deceased shall be entitled to spousal consortium, the petitioner no.2 to 4 being children of the deceased shall be entitled to parental consortium and petitioner no.5 being mother of the deceased shall be entitled to filial consortium.

Thus, the following amounts are awarded under the conventional heads:
 S. No. Conventional Head Amount  1. Spousal Consortium Rs.40,000/-
 Parental Consortium Rs.1,20,000/- 
 Filial Consortium Rs.40,000/-
 2. Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
